note: Notes are now retrievable, and a ruling is never served bare. Mechanism (convergence, not a re-target): an axis splits into ENTRIES — the current ruling block plus each note appended after it — every entry is scored independently, and the axis score is the MAX over its entries. Concatenation was rejected because clampGist is tail-biased, so a hot axis's note churn would outrank its own ruling (the objection the old note-excluding comment correctly raised); summing was rejected because it would make note COUNT a ranking advantage. Max means a note can be the hit that surfaces an axis while twenty notes buy nothing — the segment-then-max shape from SummaC (arXiv:2111.09525). Read side: rows carry qualifiedBy, prose prints the 3 most query-relevant notes plus a count, --json carries all. Qualifiers are ordered by their OWN relevance, not date: on the real frink corpus the load-bearing 'Hooks-follow PARKED' note is 4th of 20 by date, so recency ordering would have hidden exactly the note that falsifies the ruling. Measured on the seed corpus: SFER 1/1 -> 0/1, CSA 0/1 -> 1/1, Buried@5 2/3 -> 1/3. Also corrected a scorer flaw this exposed: staleness was detected by looking for supersession KEYWORDS near a stale claim, but real qualifiers use none ('PARKED', 'still blocked', 'unscheduled'), so the test is now structural — a stale claim misleads only when served without its qualifiers.

rater1Why: S2's 'strictly better than either tier' is withdrawn: matches or exceeds, beats both only on multi-axis
ruling: Both tiers run over the same candidates and are fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (score = SUM of 1/(60+rank)), K=60 from Cormack et al. 2009 and deliberately untuned at this corpus size. Fusion is strictly better than either tier on the suite: containment SINGLE 8/8, Buried-by-rank 1/8, SetRecall 3/4, PartialRecall 87.5% — beating BOTH parents on multi-axis. Abstention, however, is computed from the PRE-FUSION lexical top-1 score, never the fused score: RRF is rank-only by construction and throws away the magnitude a confidence threshold needs. Degradation to a single tier is announced on stderr, and the result's source field reports hybrid, lexical or semantic so a caller can see which path ran.

The ruling to fuse rather than ladder still holds, because the tiers demonstrably fail on different cases, but the size of the win is not established at this corpus size. Read as: matches or exceeds both tiers on every measured metric, beats both only on multi-axis.

ruling: A verdict-producing gate emits its INPUTS and its non-runs, not only its outcomes. (1) Every SELECTED reviewer emits review_scope BEFORE the judge runs — files, diff_sha256, file count and hash, and cached — so a cache hit is attributable on the same footing as a live run. (2) Every reviewer that did NOT run emits review_skipped with the reason (gate_disabled, no_llm, GUARD_REVIEW_SKIP, not_selected), so non-selection is a row and never an absence. (3) Every verdict carries prompt_identity: the same hash formula as the review-mode packaged preflight, computed over the SYNCED consumer assets on the commit/ship path, so a production rate and a bench baseline are comparable when the bytes match. (4) The per-lens checklist vector rides on review_result INCLUDING the passes, with each failing lens attributed to what the gate did with it (blocking, waived, dropped_out_of_charter). ruling: A checklist-free reviewer's prose verdict never blocks by itself. Blocking authority requires the gate to mechanically parse at least one complete finding that satisfies the reviewer's declared evidence contract. A `FAIL` without such a finding is inconclusive, preserving strict ship's fail-closed boundary without misreporting a repository-rule violation.
note: sc-3580 — the conventions evidence contract now GROUNDS each OFFENDING quote instead of only parsing it, retiring the sc-2181 bet that authoritative line counts alone would end fabricated size findings (devkit v0.62.0 blocked a consumer commit citing symbols absent from the file, on files the same length as HEAD). A pair keeps blocking authority only when (1) its path is in the reviewed set, (2) the normalized quote appears in the staged blob within ±3 lines of the cited line, or in a line the change removes (a +/- marked quote's body binds to that side of the diff, a literal staged line may itself start with -, and a +-marked quote never matches a removed line; a quote the judge wrapped across lines matches the smallest run of up to 4 joined lines), and (3) that line is part of this change: an added line, or any line of a file that grew versus HEAD (rename-aware). Grounding reads the staged tree and HEAD pinned when the judge evidence is cut, and grounds nothing whenever the index no longer holds that tree, rechecked on every grounding, runs before the path:line dedupe, and its lenses, keyed on the canonical path, are the only ones the override valve blocks on or waives. Same rule as dup-gate-evidence-verified-against-worktree; ratchets-blame-the-change-not-the-tree for size debt. Contract identity conventions-v3:grounded-quote. The conventions bench still scores syntax-only blocking authority: moving it onto grounding changes the runner and needs the freeze-and-remeasure step benchmarks-grow-from-telemetry requires, so it is a follow-up.

Default `SHIP_COMMIT_TIMEOUT` rises to 1800s with the honest full-chain equation documented; the timeout banner names the mid-flight stage + unfinished reviewers and says "re-run to converge".
note: The Ruling's '1800s' and the 2026-07-04 note's 'the 1800s ceiling is unbroken' are both STALE: run-gates-with-capture.sh has defaulted SHIP_COMMIT_TIMEOUT to 3600 since 0d759d4 (2026-07-13), which raised it with no Target and no note. Recovering the evidence rather than ratifying the drift: that commit raised the correctness reviewer's FIRST/STRICT_FIRST/ESCALATE caps 300s/420s to 30 min because its four-lens investigation legitimately ran past 420s and was SIGKILLed mid-verdict (usage-tracker showed repeated 421s inconclusive timeouts against a ~60-250s median; it was the only reviewer hitting the cap). 1800s could no longer contain one 30-min reviewer plus the fast ones, so the outer ship ceiling would have killed the chain first. 3600 is therefore the ruled value and consistent with the anchored bet — still a hang guard, not a schedule. Unchanged by this note: a judge that times out is never re-run, so a stuck judge still costs at most one cap.

rater1Why: adds: explicit ship path arguments are literal files, never pathspecs
ruling: Explicit paths remain the default for dirty-tree shipping. The opt-in --from-branch mode requires an explicit remote base, pins the base and current HEAD commits, proves ancestry, derives root-literal committed path membership, refuses in-scope overlays and unsupported path representations, and records branch source mode plus frozen membership for resume.
note: Explicit ship and reship --pr path arguments are literal files resolved from the repo root, never pathspecs (sc-2425). Each caller path reaches git as ':(literal)<path>' — WITHOUT 'top', because under git -C "$ROOT" plain literal still normalises './note.txt' while ':(top,literal)./x' matches nothing. Ambient GIT_LITERAL/GLOB/NOGLOB/ICASE_PATHSPECS are unset in both modes (literal-mode env reads the prefix as filename text; glob-mode is fatal beside it), and reconcile-manifest-write now classifies every path under --literal-pathspecs. Raw PATHS stays the storage and display identity, so receipts recorded before this change still resume. The directory refusal is framed on $ROOT like the git calls that consume the path. REJECTED: an opt-in flag for arbitrary pathspecs — no caller, test, or skill passed globs or magic, and the failure it guards is silent (reship --pr deleted every sibling a glob-named path matched). devkit reconcile reads the same manifest paths literally (git rm/checkout, rev-parse --verify), and both scrub ambient pathspec modes through literalPathspecEnv() in reconcile-manifest-write.mts. Scope: cli/lib/ship/ship-branch.sh,cli/lib/ship/reship.sh,cli/lib/ship/reconcile-manifest-write.mts,cli/lib/reconcile.mts

rater1Why: S2's 'the list is the same vocabulary review-target.sh unsets' is withdrawn: the scrub is a union bound to the ship scripts' exports
ruling: devkit own test processes inherit NO run authority from whatever launched them. vitest.setup.mjs deletes an explicit, named list of ship/review authority variables before any test module loads (setupFiles runs per worker ahead of the first import, so even a top-level process.env capture sees the cleaned env), and both vitest configs share that one file. The list is the same vocabulary cli/lib/ship/review-target.sh unsets, bound to it by a parity test so the two can never drift; membership is reused, the reason is not (that script prevents inheriting a FOREIGN run authority). Deliberate invocation knobs are never scrubbed: SHIP_COMMIT_TIMEOUT and DEVKIT_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT are inputs a caller chose. A test that needs a policy var sets it explicitly. The guarantee is about INHERITANCE, not visibility - a per-worker setup file cannot undo a test that sets a var mid-file and never restores it.
note: sc-2259 follow-up — the Target's ruling said the scrub list IS review-target.sh's vocabulary; edge-case testing showed that list is not a superset of what a ship actually exports, so the first implementation was a partial fix. ship-branch.sh additionally exports DEVKIT_SHIP_BRANCH, DEVKIT_SHIP_DRY_GATES, DEVKIT_SHIP_FROM_BRANCH, DEVKIT_SHIP_INTENT_RECORDED, DEVKIT_SHIP_PATHS, DEVKIT_SHIP_REPO, DEVKIT_SHIP_RESUMED and DEVKIT_SHIP_ROOT, none of which review-target.sh unsets because it guards a review ENTRYPOINT rather than the downstream tree. Four of those are read at runtime and are not inert: qavis-advisory shipMode() branches on DEVKIT_SHIP_ROOT and then runs git -C against that path, and review completeness verdictBranch() scopes a sticky verdict to DEVKIT_SHIP_BRANCH, so an inherited pair makes a test answer for the OUTER ship's repository. The scrub now carries three provenance lists - INHERITED_RUN_ENV (review-target.sh parity), SHIP_EXPORTED_ENV (the ship-script delta) and TEST_ONLY_ADDITIONS (the FRINK_AI_STRICT alias) - with SCRUBBED_ENV as their union. The binding test no longer trusts a hand-written list: it parses the export left-hand sides out of ship-branch.sh and run-gates-with-capture.sh and requires every DEVKIT_/GUARD_ name found there to be scrubbed, so a future ship export is caught at the source rather than after it flips a gate test. Also pinned: vitest.e2e.config.mjs shares the same setupFiles, which was assumed rather than asserted.

rater1Why: S1's 'into devkit's own skills/ tree' is replaced: the vendored skill lives in .devkit/vendored-skills/
ruling: Vendor third-party agent assets into devkit's own skills/ tree, pinned by FULL upstream commit SHA plus a sha256 of the vendored bytes (cli/lib/install/vendored-skills.mts, asserted by vendored-skills.test.mts). Delegating to the upstream installer ('claude plugin marketplace add' + 'claude plugin install') is REJECTED: Claude-only, writes to the user's GLOBAL config rather than the repo, needs the network at install time, and cannot be drift-checked or deselected. A SHA rather than a version range because these upstreams publish no tags — the SHA is the only stable identifier for the bytes that were reviewed. The upstream LICENSE ships BESIDE the asset rather than being folded into its frontmatter: that satisfies MIT attribution while keeping the asset byte-identical to upstream, so the recorded hash stays an exact upstream comparison. Pin refreshes are a deliberate maintainer act via scripts/sync-vendored-skills.mjs (network; never called by init/upgrade).
note: The vendored skill now installs to .devkit/vendored-skills/<name>/, NOT the agent skills dirs. .claude/skills/ (and its Cursor/Codex twins) is where the CONSUMER's hand-authored skills live; a pinned third-party copy devkit owns, drift-checks and reclaims does not belong sitting among them, indistinguishable from the reader's own work. Delivery is now a plain two-file copy (cli/lib/install/adhd-skill.mts) called from init and the overlay, so the component no longer depends on skills being on, and skillNamesForSelection returns a constant false for the name — that exclusion is ALSO the whole migration, since syncSkills' existing manifest reclamation deletes a previously-manifested skill dir the moment it leaves the selected set (verified on both surfaces against both the v2 and legacy manifest schemas). No bespoke upgrade step. .devkit/ was chosen over a new top-level dir because devkit already owns that tree: clean removes it wholesale and the overlay git-exclude already covers it, so the relocation added no removal or ignore machinery — only a doctor presence-check, replacing the drift coverage the skills manifest used to provide indirectly. Cost: /i-have-adhd no longer resolves as a slash command (skill discovery only scans the agent skills dirs), so the SessionStart hook is now the ONLY way it runs — acceptable because the skill sets disable-model-invocation and the 2026-07-30 note already made the hook its only real entry point; the loss is re-invoking it by hand after 'stop adhd mode'. Reclaim here is deliberately NOT pristine-checked, unlike the agent skills dirs: clean already deletes .devkit/ unconditionally, so honouring a local edit in one path but not the other would be the inconsistency rather than the safeguard. REJECTED again, more specifically than on 2026-07-29: shipping it as a real Claude Code plugin (.claude/plugins/<name>/ + enabledPlugins), the shape frink's ponytail-frink uses. Enabling ANY plugin — project-scoped or not — records marketplace and install state in the USER's global ~/.claude/plugins/*.json and loads from a versioned global cache, which is the same global-config objection that killed the upstream installer; activation also needs a committed extraKnownMarketplaces key that would turn a personal reading preference into a team-wide default and write into every teammate's home dir — the exact inversion of gitignoring .devkit/adhd-off.
